Silesia organisers list Warholm among confirmed stars; dos Santos is not listed. Warholm ran a world-leading 46.61 in London on Jul 18 while dos Santos skipped it. Dos Santos is healthy (racing Troféu Brasil Jul 23-26) and is 3-0 vs Warholm in 2026, but his Silesia start is uncertain.

The Diamond League confirmed an Alfred v Jefferson-Wooden 100m clash at Silesia, and both are on the meet's confirmed list along with Swoboda. Alfred has been dominant in 2026 (200m wins in Monaco 21.51 and London 21.66). MJW won the Pre 100m on Jul 4 over Richardson.

Open field. 2026 Slams went to Rybakina (AO), Andreeva (RG) and Noskova (Wimbledon). Sabalenka is still No. 1 and the US Open defending champion, Swiatek won Cincinnati 2025, and Muchova is out of Toronto after surgery (Jul 19). Andreeva nudged up.

Sinner has won all 5 Masters in 2026 plus Wimbledon (Jul 12) and is entered. Alcaraz, the defending champion, has entered Cincinnati (Reuters Jul 16) as his first event since April after a wrist injury. Zverev won RG and was the Wimbledon runner-up.

Mercedes have won 8 of 10 races. Antonelli won Belgium on Jul 19 from his 6th pole (6 wins in total) and leads the standings. Russell had car issues and crashed out at Spa. Leclerc won Silverstone. Verstappen was P2 in Austria and on the Spa front row, and Zandvoort is his home race; he replaces the struggling Norris.

Lincoln set a record of 210+ days at sea with no port call since Guam (Dec 11-12), and crew-welfare concerns were reported Jul 9. The war resumed and the blockade was reimposed Jul 14-15, so it stays in the Arabian Sea with the Bush. Options are a regional rest stop (Oman; Gulf ports risky under Iranian strikes), a Med rest stop like the Ford's (Greece), or the transit home (Singapore, Guam/Hawaii).
